Cancelable intent event with `open` and `reason` (escape, outside, close-button, close-watcher, request, trigger). Preventing it keeps the dialog as it is. `tct-after-open-change` follows once the animation settled.
A number is px, a string a CSS length; clamped to the viewport gutter.
Object `{top, bottom, start, end}`; `start` and `end` are logical and mirror in RTL. Property only (A§7.2 data props).

api.reason: A-xstyle: use class/style, ::part(dialog) and ::part(content), --dialog-padding, and the padding, width and max-height attributes.

api.notes: Asks like the user does (cancelable tct-open-change). `show()`, `hide()` and `toggle()` change it programmatically without an intent event.

hooks.notes: Escape, backdrop press and platform close requests go through the shared layer stack, innermost first, with the dialog's purpose as its dismissal policy.
The controller locks page scroll while a modal is open (with scrollbar-gutter: stable, so the page does not shift).
`openDialog(content, options)` from @tecton-wc/components/dialog/dialog.api.js returns a handle {element, isOpen, hide(), closed}.

keyboard.action: Asks to close the innermost dialog (tooltips first). Not for purpose=required; a composing IME Escape is claimed and ignored.
Stays inside the modal: the page behind is inert.

keyboard.keys: Enter or Space on the close button
keyboard.action: Asks to close with reason close-button.

differences.text: `heading` and `subtitle` attributes (and a `heading` slot) are shorthand for a tct-dialog-header as first child; upstream composes DialogHeader in the children. Composing tct-dialog-header directly works and names the dialog the same way.

The dialog pads its own content (`--dialog-padding`, or the `padding` step) because there is no Layout element yet; upstream delegates padding to Layout. Once tct-layout exists, the same value is republished as `--_dialog-padding`.
Required accessible name: a `heading`, a header, or an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on the host (mirrored onto the `<dialog>`); the dialog warns once in dev mode when it opens without one.

Declarative invokers work: `<button commandfor="dlg" command="--show">` (also `--hide`, `--toggle`) through the platform's invoker commands where present and a document-level click fallback elsewhere. The invoker gets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

The `<dialog>` is the modal in the top layer, so the page behind is inert and needs no focus trap or portal. The announcer's live regions move into the top-most modal, so toast-like messages are still spoken while a modal is open.

Drawn with a rule around it, the container radius (8px) and the high elevation shadow (tecton-astryx components.ts `dialog`); entry is a rise from the opener's side with a fade, only a fade under reduced motion.
`openDialog()` is a module function rather than a hook; it renders a `tct-dialog` into the page, opens it and removes it once it has closed.
A `required` dialog ignores user dismissal only: `requestClose()`, `hide()` and a `<form method="dialog">` in the content still close it (an explicit action of the application).

provisional: Entry animation distance (16px rise, scale 0.95) and the 2px backdrop blur are upstream's values and were not re-tuned for Tecton.
core.dialog.notes: Guides: [mwg:light-dismiss-a-dialog] backdrop press through the layer stack, per purpose; [mwg:platform-controls-dismiss-dialog] `cancel` and CloseWatcher requests respect the escape policy; [mwg:declarative-dialog-popover-control] commandfor/command invokers; [mwg:animate-to-from-top-layer] WAAPI exit before `close()` (never `overlay`); [mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui] live regions inside the modal; [mwg:move-dom-element-without-losing-state] moveBefore keeps the dialog modal; [mwg:accessible-web-components] name from the heading via ids.

api.notes: Rendered as an <h2> satellite in the light DOM (tabindex -1); `slot="title"` takes an element of your own. `title` is a global attribute, so it is not reused (A§7.1).

Inside a tct-dialog the close button asks the dialog; on its own the header fires the cancelable event itself (open false, reason close-button). Without the close button (no-close-button, or purpose=required) there is none.
Upstream defaults to true; see DIALOG-HEADER-01.

api.reason: A-xstyle: use class/style and the ::part(...) list of the header.

differences.text: `has-divider` defaults to off: the Tecton dialog reads as one surface with a rule around it, and a rule under the title is asked for, not the default.

The close button is shown by default (upstream only when `onOpenChange` is passed) and turned off with `no-close-button`; a purpose=required dialog never shows it. Its label is localised ("Close") and `close-label` overrides it. It is a tct-button (ghost, icon-only) whose built-in tooltip shows the label.
The heading is a real <h2> in the light DOM so the dialog (whose <dialog> is in a shadow root) can name itself with an id reference, and it takes focus when a modal opens without becoming a tab stop.

core.dialog-header.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] the heading satellite and id references; [mwg:custom-button-actions] the close button asks instead of closing.
